purpose: Measure post-stop interactions and partition changes in fixed-graph DW; no novelty or confirmatory claim.
initialization: Independent uniform [0,1) opinions; graph, opinion and event RNG streams explicitly recorded. No graph rejection or resampling.
schedule: After receptive events, t>0, adaptive check interval 10**(floor(log10(t))-3), initialized to zero; mirrors reference scheduling with Tmin=0 and sigfigs=3.
budget_rule: After the 10 benchmark trajectories, choose the largest allowed pilot cap whose worst-case duration for 128 pilot+sensitivity trajectories is <=1200 seconds using the slowest measured attempts/second. If none fits, do not launch the batch; record a linked budget revision. Use the same cap for sensitivity. Timing only, not observed effects, determines this choice.
primary_outcomes: First receptive interaction crossing each declared partition after its stopping time
Partition difference and component size/count change at certified or censored endpoint
Attempt counts to each stopping rule, with right censoring and numerical failures explicit
decision_rule: Proceed beyond this pilot only if controls and numerical invariants pass and effects occur beyond the constructed case, changing an interpretable contrast or delimiting a useful reliability region. Zero observed failures with this small nested sample does not establish a population bound. Do not add configurations to obtain a positive finding.
limitations: Reduced independent implementation; no claim to reproduce published aggregate figures or campaign inputs
Interval separation has prior literature; graph-local variant has no established novelty
Same trajectory per stopping-rule comparison; common random uniforms across model arms do not imply identical edge sequences
Graphs are nested units; four trials in each cell are not four independent graph realizations
Sensitivity reuses a fixed subset of pilot inputs and has a different stopping tolerance
Finite arithmetic certificate uses a conservative 1e-12 gap margin, not interval arithmetic over an entire exact trajectory
